notes:
Account summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS. Primary goal is to add LLM-based support assistant + semantic search across product docs and changelogs. Started on Hosted API (trial) -> good dev velocity -> now evaluating Dedicated for predictable cost and data isolation.

Key stakeholders: Head of Product (Lena Morales), CTO (Samir Kapoor), Procurement lead (J. O'Neill), Security (Dir. InfoSec: Priya Narang). AE: Avery Chen. SE: Diego Ramos. CSM tentatively assigned (post-contract): Maya Singh.

POC history & outcomes:
- 2026-01-25: Intro demo (hosted API) — ran sample chat flows, embedding prototype. Feedback: latency OK for dev traffic, want deterministic 95th p50/p95 numbers.
- 2026-02-02: 2-week POC spun on Hosted API — used smaller prompt pipelines, 100k tokens/day peak. Success criteria: (1) 95th latency <250ms for chat, (2) embedding cosine drift <1% vs baseline, (3) docs retrieval relevance >0.72 MAP.
- 2026-02-18: POC results review (Fireflies id ff_2026-02-18_arterra_kickoff) — satisfied quality, flagged cost variability and multi-tenant isolation concerns. SE proposed Dedicated with VPC peering, reserved capacity sizing options.
- 2026-03-03: Legal kickoff call (ff_2026-03-03_legal_review_call) — procurement requested MSA/DPA redlines and SOC2 evidence.

Technical requirements / constraints:
- Workloads: chat (conversational support agent), embeddings (semantic search index), reranking for search results.
- Latency target: p95 chat <200-250ms for primary region (NA).
- Throughput: peak expected 50-80 concurrent chat sessions, ~60 req/s for embedding batch jobs during nightly indexing windows.
- Model preferences: prefer open models hosted via Redwood with ability to pin versions; fallback to smaller quantized variants under load.
- Routing/fallback: want canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to 1-2 cheaper model variants when Dedicated capacity saturated.
- Deployment: require VPC peering, customer-managed KMS for key wrapping, audit logging to be forwarded to SIEM, and option to enable on-prem connector later.

Security / compliance asks from InfoSec:
- Provide SOC2 Type II report and SSP (done) — InfoSec requested last 12 months coverage.
- DPA redlines: data residency clause should permit US & EU residency constraints for different customer segments.
- Retention: ability to set retention policies per dataset; default retention 1 year for logs, ability to purge on termination.
- SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning required for initial 50 seats.
- KMS integration: customer-managed keys required for model input encryption at rest.

Contract and procurement notes:
- Procurement wants standard MSA but will redline: indemnity, liability cap (they push for mutual cap at 1x ARR; Redwood standard is lower), termination for convenience (30 vs 90 days), data deletion & export clauses.
- DPA: wants explicit subprocessor list and 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
- SLA: customer asking 99.9% uptime with credits; also wants p95 latency SLOs for chat in contract and a clear credit formula. SE already proposed options for Dedicated tiers (S1/S2/S3) with measurable SLOs.
- Pricing: initial committed reserved capacity estimate = 40k tokens/day baseline, with burst policy to 120k tokens/day; procurement asked for committed discount schedule and overage rates. Initial ARR estimate ~200k/yr if Dedicated signed.

- Legal: MSA redlines incoming (Arterra legal) — need Redwood legal to produce counter (Owner: Avery).
- SLA license: define credit formula and latency SLOs for p95 (Owner: Diego + Product).
- KMS onboarding: confirm KMS provider compatibility (AWS KMS vs Azure KeyVault) and integration timeline (Owner: SE).
- Finance: needs PO process and taxpayer information for E-invoice (Owner: Procurement).
